title: Quarterly Opera: Sprint guide for Hosted API + Model Catalog convergence
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Playbook and sprint-level plan to align Hosted API feature roadmap with model catalog curation and rotation for Q2. Focus areas: canary windows, model tiering, capacity hedges, eval gating, and console UX to surface model health. Deliver a schedule and runbook that PM, Eng, Design, and SRE can execute against.
objective: Reduce model rollout toil and rollout-related incidents by 50% while enabling two staggered model rotations for high-demand endpoints within the quarter.
okrs: O1: Improve rollout reliability — KR1: Decrease rollout incidents tied to model swaps by 50% (baseline q1)
O1: Improve rollout reliability — KR2: Establish canary windows and automated telemetry checks for 100% of hosted model swaps
O2: Cost & performance — KR1: Identify top 10 endpoints and implement cost-saving quantization/parallelization recommendations with >=10% unit-cost reduction
O3: Developer experience — KR1: Publish step-by-step canary playbook and console UI shortcut; achieve 90% satisfaction in internal alpha
milestones: M2: Draft canary gating criteria and telemetry checks (target 2026-03-15)
M3: Console UX mock and quicklink for model health (target 2026-03-22)
M4: Pilot rotation for 2 low-risk endpoints (target 2026-04-05)
M5: Full rotation runbook + run of 2 medium-risk endpoints (target 2026-04-25)
acceptance_criteria: A1: Canary automation triggers on metric regressions (latency, 95th p99 errors, model-quality evals)
A2: Console shows per-route model health with direct action buttons for rollback and annotate
A3: Two model rotations performed with zero customer-facing errors and documented rollback timestamps
A4: Playbook published in Confluence and referenced in on-call runbooks
risks: R1: Model-eval regressions that only manifest under production distribution (mitigation: canary traffic slicing and offline evaluation mirror)
R2: Capacity contention during simultaneous rotations (mitigation: reserved hedges + progressive rollout windows)
R3: Incomplete telemetry for older endpoints (mitigation: quick instrumentation spike during pilot)
R4: Console actionability gaps could slow rollbacks (mitigation: keyboard shortcuts + API endpoints for ops automation)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive batching/quantization reduces cost but increases risk of subtle quality drift; team agreed phase-gated profile testing before catalog-wide recommendations.
We will limit initial rotations to endpoints flagged as 'non-critical' in the endpoint-runbook table and maintain a fallback model variant list per route.
Consideration: tie rotation windows to regional capacity to avoid cross-region degradation. Ops to provide capacity forecast by 2026-03-12.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff workshop completed. Agreement: two-track pilot (low-risk then medium-risk). Action items assigned to Eng (canary infra) and Analytics (baseline dashboards).
2026-03-04: Design submitted UX first-pass. PM feedback: make rollback CTA omnipresent on per-route pages. Design to iterate by 03/10.
2026-03-08: Eng spike for canary gating finished. Found gap in metric collection for legacy endpoints; SRE to add instrumentation scope (ETA 03/14).
2026-03-10: Cost model shows top 10 endpoints account for 62% of token spend; prioritizing 3 endpoints for early optimization.
2026-03-11: Decided to require automated eval pass for any model variant promoted to canary. Draft gating rules uploaded to Confluence.
comments: Marco Alvarez: Added note to include canary-specific runbook steps for on-call during rotations.
